M1.location: src/mvh/stages/spectral/dsp.py select_kick_events / select_hit_events (refractory 0.2 s, low-band step 6.5 dB / excess 3.5 dB rules)
M1.claim: Not fixed, and worse. On the contract fixture song, kick events fail PLAN §7 (F1 >= 0.95 at +-10 ms). The cause is not hats. Bass-note onsets (truth notes.bass, midi 29/33, 44-55 Hz, inside the viz kick band) 100 ms before a kick are emitted as kicks (viz true). The real kick after each one falls inside the refractory and is dropped: over the held bass its <=400 Hz excess is only 2-4 dB.
M1.evidence:
- Fixture song: F1 0.864 (P 0.835, R 0.894), 91 events for 85 kicks. Round 2 had 0.880.
- Missed kicks at 9.9, 11.9, 15.9, 20.4, 22.4 and 24.4 s each have their nearest event at -0.10 s, which is the bass-note onset.
- kick_glide separates the two: lost kicks 1.93-2.25 at 8 of 9; the pre-empting bass onsets 0.48-0.80 at 6 of 7. The docstring promises rules that use it (glide_song, refractory override), but they are not implemented.
- The round-1 floor test (P >= 0.85, R >= 0.9) now fails too.
- Probe: out/_wip/r-dsp-m1-r3/dbg_fix.py.
M1.suggested_fix:
- Do not let a candidate without the kick-body pitch drop (low kick_glide) open a refractory over a following candidate that has it.
- Judge the kick's own attack on the kick band (about 30-120 Hz, zero-phase), not on <=400 Hz where bass harmonics dominate.
- Use kick_glide in kick_conf.

M1.location: src/mvh/stages/spectral/dsp.py select_kick_events (<=400 Hz low-band 'own attack' plus refractory); tests/unit/spectral test_kick_events_with_sub_bass_line (bar lowered)
M1.claim: Regression from the B1-R2 fix. A <=400 Hz step belongs as much to the bass instrument as to the kick. Over a moving bass line, bass-note onsets are emitted as kicks with kick_conf up to 1.0, and through the refractory they suppress real kicks up to 363 ms later. The fixer lowered the builder's own unit-test recall bar from 0.85 to 0.7 so the test would pass.
M1.evidence:
- Builder's tests/synth/m1/signals.groove():
  - default: F1 0.754 (P 0.780, R 0.730), 59 events for 63 kicks
  - seed 3: F1 0.739
  - straight four-on-the-floor with off-beat bass: F1 0.880, with 12 extras at kick_conf 1.0
  - without the bass: 0.976 / 1.0
- 16th-note bass riff under four-on-the-floor: the G1 note one 16th before each downbeat is emitted as a kick in every bar. 40 events for 32 kicks, F1 0.889.
- Probes: probe_groove2.py, probe_r3.py.
M1.suggested_fix:
- Compute the kick's own attack on the kick band, not <=400 Hz.
- Gate the refractory on kick_glide (see B1-R2).
- Restore the unit-test bar to PLAN §7 (F1 >= 0.95) and add groove(seed=3) and the 16th riff to the unit tests.

M1.location: src/mvh/stages/spectral/dsp.py select_kick_events roll rule (own step >= 6.5 dB, excess >= 3.5 dB, click >= 15 dB)
M1.claim: Fixed only at the tested tempo. The fixed-dB roll rule is tuned to the one tested case: 16th double kicks fail above 160 BPM or under a cymbal, which masks the required >= 1 kHz click. Metal double bass plays 160-220 BPM, usually under cymbals.
M1.evidence:
- Tight clicky kick on 16ths, 96 kicks:
  - 150 and 160 BPM: 96/96
  - 170 BPM: 78/96 (F1 0.897)
  - 180 BPM: 3/96 (F1 0.061)
  - 200 BPM: 1/96
  - 160 BPM under a crash every 2 s: 42/96 (F1 0.609)
  - the fixture's longer kick at 160 BPM: 24/96
- Probe: probe_r3.py.
M1.suggested_fix:
- Take dense-roll kicks from the low-band or kick-band envelope, with thresholds relative to the local inter-onset level, not fixed dB.

M2.location: src/mvh/stages/structure/features.py bar_pattern (slot edges) + src/mvh/stages/structure/__init__.py (merge guard merge_keep_strong, dyn gate); tests/review/M2/r-dsp/test_structure_real_upstream.py harness (fixture rhythm)
M2.claim: F4-r2 is fixed only for the fixture's exact truth rhythm. With the real rhythm (beats F1 1.0, two downbeats 18 ms late), the structure stage again misplaces sections on the synthetic song, and a 10 ms bar shift flips the result. The review test passes because the fixture rhythm is the truth rhythm, a third circular input.
M2.evidence:
Full pipeline: a fresh mvh analyze of the synthetic song (out/_wip/r-dsp-m2-r3/synth) gives sections 0.99/5.0/9.0/17.0/25.0/34.5/50.52 s, boundary F 0.923. The intro is split 2+2 bars at 5.0 s and both halves are in group A.

Causal input (p_full.py): swapping ONLY the real rhythm events into the recorded real allin1 + harmony + dynamics harness reproduces F 0.923. Swapping chroma, dynamics or allin1 alone leaves F at 1.0. The real bars are within 5 ms of truth except at 7.018 s and 50.518 s (+18 ms).

Feature sensitivity: nov_pat at 5.0 s rises from 0.42 to 0.59 and the score from 2.34 to 2.47, crossing the same-group merge guard 1.4 x cost = 2.41.

Shift probe (p_jitter.py): shifting the truth bars by a constant -10 ms splits the bridge 2+3 at 29.0 s (F 0.923).

Mechanism (p_pattern.py): bar_pattern slot edges fall exactly on the 16th-note grid, so a bar that starts one frame late moves every hit to the previous slot. Identical bars then get cosine 0.0.

Dynamics gate: dyn_gate 0.7 is below the median own score (about 25/28 bars saturate), so dynamics adds +0.75 at 5.0 s.

The new test fails 3 of 5:
- real rhythm: F 0.923
- -10 ms shift: F 0.923
- bar_pattern jitter: cosine 0.0
The precondition test (rhythm within tolerance) and the +10 ms shift pass.
M2.suggested_fix: Centre the bar_pattern slots on the grid positions (offset the edges by half a slot) or use soft or overlapping pooling, so 1-2 frames of downbeat jitter do not change the fingerprint. Make the same-group merge guard less of a knife edge, for example with hysteresis or by requiring a clear margin over cost. Gate the dynamics evidence relative to the section cost. Score the structure tests with the recorded real rhythm (data/synth_real_rhythm.npz) and with ±10-20 ms bar jitter, not only with the fixture rhythm.

M2.location: src/mvh/stages/structure/__init__.py: repeat grouping (agglomerative, F4-r2 fix) feeding the same-group merge; EDM drop extent rule (while drive[j+1] >= drive[i] - 0.6, i = the drop's first section)
M2.claim: Regression from the F4-r2 fix on MEGAFAUNA, the module's named regression song: the drop now ends at 176.1 s instead of 212.7 s. Three loud-plateau sections (176.1, 185.3, 194.4 s) are labelled 'inst', against SPIKE's 'loud plateau 146-217 s', and the drop's repeat groups now mix drop and inst sections of the same material and energy.
M2.evidence:
Replay with cached W0 logits, rhythm unchanged since r2 (out/_wip/r-dsp-m2-r3/replay vs r-dsp-m2-r2/replay):
- r2: build 123.5-141.8, drop 141.8-212.7.
- r3: drop 141.8-176.1.

Cause: the bar at 151.0 s scores above cost in both rounds (r2 1.10 vs 0.80, r3 1.61 vs 1.11). The new grouping places 151.0 in group K (with 176.1/185.3) instead of J, so the merge no longer rejoins 141.8+151.0. The drop's first section is now 4 bars at drive 2.49 z (8-bar: 2.19), which raises the extension bar from 1.59 to 1.89. The plateau sections at 1.73/1.62/1.90 z drop out: 151.0 s at 1.895 z is a drop, while 194.4 s at 1.898 z is inst.

Neither split_min_novelty 0 nor repeat_adjacent_penalty 1.0 restores it (p_mega.py).

Test (-m real): drop cover of 146.3-212 s is 0.45 (needs >= 0.9).
M2.suggested_fix: Make the drop extent independent of segmentation granularity: compare following sections against the drop's peak-plateau level (for example a bar-level drive threshold relative to the song's drive distribution, or the max over the first 8 bars), and extend over sections in the same repeat group as the drop's opening. Keep roles consistent within a repeat group (a group that contains a drop section should not label the same material 'inst' at equal energy).

M3a.location: src/mvh/stages/drums/core.py drumsep_hits (cymbal_rise_db=8.0, applied as the detect() rise floor for the ride and crash sub-stems)
M3a.claim: Ride and crash candidates need a broadband rise of 8 dB. A ride played in 8th notes rises only 6.4-6.5 dB over the ring of the previous stroke, so about 95 % of the strokes are lost, even on clean sub-stems. The synthetic song has only quarter-note rides 0.5 s apart, so the PLAN §7 cymbal gate never exercises a ride pattern.
M3a.evidence:
One clean ride stroke from the generator, tiled at a uniform spacing, through core.drumsep_hits:
- 8th notes at 140 bpm: recall .057 (2/35), lowest rises 6.5 dB.
- 8th notes at 150 bpm: recall .053 (2/38), lowest rises 6.4 dB.
- 8th notes at 120 bpm: recall .967 (the rise is 8.2 dB, just over the floor).
- With cymbal_rise_db=4: recall 1.0 and precision 1.0 at 100-150 bpm.
- A ride with dynamics fails the same way: every other quarter-note stroke 6 dB down rises 7.5 dB, and ride recall is .56.

End to end, the synthetic mix with its ride part doubled at +0.214 s through ingest..drums on ROCm (out/_wip/r-ml-m3a-r3/variants/synth_ride8): ride recall .219 (7/32), song cymbal F1 .385 against the .7 gate.
M3a.suggested_fix:
- Detect ride and crash onsets on the 4-16 kHz band, as detect_air does for hats, or set the rise floor from the stem's own ODF spread instead of a fixed 8 dB.
- Keep the precision on separated stems with the ring and leak rules that already exist.
- Add a synthetic 8th-note and 16th-note ride, with accents, to the module tests, both on clean sub-stems and end to end.

M4.location: src/mvh/stages/harmony/keys.py global_confidence (sources set / len(sources) < 2 cap); core.analyse_key ignores the lv-chordia no-chord share
M4.claim: M1's remaining half: when lv-chordia reports 100% no-chord, the key is still not marked as having no tonal evidence. Any input where S-KEY clears its 0.2 vote gate gets a confident key with no low-confidence flag, including noise, drones, risers and ambient pads.
M4.evidence: Band-limited (300-700 Hz) 60 s noise. Real lv-chordia: no-chord share 1.0. Real S-KEY: recovered p_max 0.41 on F minor, so it votes. Sources are {skey, profiles}, which is 2, so the cap does not fire. Result: 'F minor' at confidence 0.80 (0.708 in the probe out/_wip/r-ml-m4-r3/probe_extra.log, case band60), with flags ['key:methods_disagree'] only and no key:low_confidence or key:no_tonal_evidence. The test fails now in both variants: the stub S-KEY at 0.41 gives 0.792 and the real S-KEY gives 0.802.
M4.suggested_fix: Gate the key on tonal evidence from the chord model. If the lv-chordia no-chord share in the span is about 0.9 or higher, cap confidence at about 0.3 and add key:no_tonal_evidence, whatever S-KEY says. Also count chords and phrase as a source only when the non-N share is above a floor (this fixes m13 too). Add unit tests for these paths.

M5.claim: LRC ID tags no longer mark a file as labelled, and headers that contain an instrumental word no longer name a speaker. Two cases from R2-1 are still open. (1) _header recognises a section only when the section word comes first (low.startswith(SECTION_WORDS)). So [Pre Chorus] (no hyphen), [Post Chorus], [Final Chorus], [Last Chorus] and [Rap Verse] are read as speaker names. These headers recur, so the file counts as labelled, the following lines carry them as hints, and voices forces k from the hints on a one-singer song. (2) A chorus line written out twice that starts with 'Time:' counts as a recurring label, so the sung word 'Time' is cut from every chorus.
M5.evidence: test_rw5_r3_speaker_labels.py: 6 tests fail and the guard passes. Failures: the section headers become the hints ['Post Chorus', 'Pre Chorus', 'Time'], so voices would force k = 3; '[Final Chorus] is read as speaker Final Chorus' (the same for [Rap Verse] and [Last Chorus]); with the chorus written out twice the lines start ['it', 'Carry', ...] with hints ['Time', 'Time', ...].
M5.suggested_fix: Treat a header as a section when ANY of its words is a section word (also match 'pre chorus' / 'post chorus' without the hyphen). Do not count an inline label as recurring when it prefixes the same line text each time (a repeated lyric, not a change of speaker). Require at least 2 distinct recurring labels before a bare-header file counts as labelled.

M5.location: src/mvh/stages/lyrics/asr.py::_generic_suspect (M5-D37 second signal no_speech_prob > 0.4; R2-3 only partly fixed)
M5.claim: Generic outro phrases ('see you (in the) next', 'please like/share', bare 'bye' / 'goodbye' / 'thank you') still drop a whole confident sung segment in the middle of active vocals. The second signal no_speech_prob > 0.4 is the normal state for sung 30 s windows: faster-whisper computes no_speech_prob once per window, and singing pushes it up.
M5.evidence: Cached W0 whisper output (counts only). Among the confident segments (mean word p >= 0.8, avg_logprob > -0.5), no_speech_prob is above 0.4 in 11 of 25 on jeremy (0.67 / 0.78) and in 21 of 48 on newton (0.42). test_rw5_r3_hallucination_nospeech.py: 6 tests fail. Each drops a segment with p 0.9 and logprob -0.3 at 60 s inside active vocals as {'non_lyric_tag': 1} when no_speech_prob is 0.67 or 0.425. The 2 guards pass: the real hallucinations are still dropped.
M5.suggested_fix: Do not use no_speech_prob alone as the second signal. Use it only together with avg_logprob < -1 or mean word p < 0.6, as the general filter does, or rely on vocal activity / position at the audio edges. Never drop a confident segment inside active vocals.

M5.location: src/mvh/stages/lyrics/text.py::_header (':' split takes the text after the colon) and _LABEL_RE (needs text after the colon)
M5.claim: Two common speaker-marker formats in user-supplied battle lyrics lose the speaker. (1) In '[Name:]' the speaker is taken from the empty text after the colon, so it is None and no line gets a hint. (2) 'Name:' alone on its own line is not a label; it becomes a SUNG lyric line, which is aligned, exported and counted in G1-G4 and in the mouth gate. Speaker hints from the text are the only route to n_source 'hints' for the rap battle, the stress test.
M5.evidence: test_rw5_r3_battle_label_formats.py has 2 failing tests and 1 passing guard; the battle uses 6 turns and 4 names. [bracket_name_colon]: hints are all None (12 lines). [name_colon_line]: 6 speaker-marker lines become sung lyric lines (18 lines for 12 verse lines). The guard [Verse: Name] format still works.
M5.suggested_fix: In _header, when the text after the colon is empty, use the text before the colon as the speaker (unless it is a section word or a metadata key). Treat a line that is only a short capitalised name followed by ':' as a speaker marker, not a lyric line, in the same way that a bare [Name] header is treated.

M5.location: src/mvh/stages/lyrics/text.py::parse_txt (section headers only recognised inside [...] / {...} via _HEADER_RE)
M5.claim: Section headers without brackets in user-supplied or embedded plain-text lyrics become sung lyric lines: 'Verse 1:', 'Chorus:', 'Bridge:', 'VERSE 1' / 'CHORUS' in capitals, 'Chorus x2' (which becomes TWO lines 'Chorus'), and '(Chorus)' (which becomes a backing lyric line instead of re-inserting the chorus). The header words are force-aligned onto the vocals and written to lyrics.json, to every caption export and to the mouth gate. The grade gate does not notice, and no warning is given.
M5.evidence: End-to-end runs on the synthetic song with the truth lyrics plus headers (out/_wip/r-words-m5-r3/synth-plainhdr and synth-capshdr): grade A, coverage 0.914, no warning, 14 lines / 58 words against the truth of 10 / 53. 'Verse 1:' is placed at 9.0 s, 'Chorus:' at 16.92 s, 'Bridge:' at 24.0 s and '(Chorus)' at 29.76 s, and all of them appear in lyrics.srt. test_rw5_r3_unbracketed_headers.py: 5 tests fail (colon, caps, chorus_x2, paren_chorus, plus '(Chorus) did not re-insert the chorus'); the guard passes ('Chorus of angels ...' stays a lyric).
M5.suggested_fix: In parse_txt, treat a line as a header when the whole line is a section word with an optional number, colon, 'xN' or parentheses (for example ^\(?(verse|chorus|bridge|pre-?chorus|hook|intro|outro|refrain)\s*\d*\s*:?\s*(x\s*\d)?\)?$, any case). Treat '(Chorus)' like '(Repeat chorus)'. Optionally warn when an aligned line consists only of section words.

M6a.location: src/mvh/assets/viewer/edit.js save() failure branch (`if (isUndo) st.history.push(J(clean(prev)))`) and undo()
M6a.claim: When an Undo's POST fails, save() pushes the CURRENT document back onto the history instead of the entry undo() popped. The state Undo was restoring is lost. The next Undo rewrites the current state ('Saved: undo', nothing changes) and the Undo after it skips a step, so a correction is silently discarded. This is the same symptom as F-R2-UNDO, reached through the fixer's new failure branch.
M6a.evidence:
1. Headless Edge, CDP scenario 'undo-fail': edits of 10, 20 and 30 ms, then one Undo whose POST is answered 503, then Undo, Undo. On disk: [0.03, 0.01], expected [0.02, 0.01]. Same result in two separate gate runs.
2. That 503 is what mvh view really answers on Windows when overrides.json is read-only or locked: out/_wip/r-platform-m6a-r3/probe_ro.py returned '503 could not write overrides.json (PermissionError)' after 13.2 s.
3. With no server fault, in Claude_Browser on the served synth folder: two Ctrl+Z presses 5 ms apart made the second Undo 409 on the stale etag. The following Ctrl+Z presses gave 0.02, 0.02 (no change) and then null, so the 0.01 state was skipped.
M6a.suggested_fix: Have undo() pass the entry it popped to save() (e.g. save(doc, 'undo', poppedEntry)), and have the failure branch push back that entry, not J(clean(prev)). Also ignore or queue Undo and Ctrl+Z while st.saving, so a second Undo never goes out with a stale etag.

M6b.claim: The template's own palette hint (`palette: []   # hex (#1b2a49) or colour words`) leads users to type `[#c93523, night blue]`. In YAML that is a ParserError, so the whole template is dropped and the user's characters and do_not rules are lost. Fenced: the status goes back to pending. Unfenced: the file falls back to free text with the R3-2 junk.
M6b.evidence: test_hex_palette_as_the_template_hint_shows_keeps_the_answers[fenced/unfenced] fails: do_not loses 'never show faces', C1 is not named 'Keeper' and the palette lacks #c93523. The r-words R3 test test_rw3_template_hex.py found the same independently.
M6b.suggested_fix: Quote hex values before loading (or pre-process `[#...` inside flow lists), show a quoted example in the hint (`["#1b2a49", night blue]`), and on a ParserError parse the template line by line so the other answers are kept.

M6b.location: src/mvh/stages/meaning/intent.py parse_intent free-text fallback (reopens R2-2 / N3)
M6b.claim: When the unfenced template does not parse (R3-1, or a template without the '# mvh-intent' marker plus any `Key:` note), the file is re-read as free text and the template's example comments become user claims. `line_singers: # ... {L005: C1+C2}` gives L005 to C1+C2 at user precedence, and the hint makes #1b2a49 the user's palette.
M6b.evidence: test_template_example_comments_never_become_user_claims[hex_palette] and [no_marker_plus_note] fail: intent.line_singers contains L005, meaning.palette contains #1b2a49 with field_sources user, and events/singing.json L005 has source 'user'.
M6b.suggested_fix: Never feed template-shaped lines (YAML comment lines, `key:   # ...` lines, flow maps) to the free-text parser. Strip each template line's trailing `# ...` comment before free-text parsing.

M6b.location: src/mvh/stages/meaning/intent.py _parse_text do-not label block (regression from the N2 fix)
M6b.claim: A do-not label line (`Never show: blood`, `Avoid: lens flares`) opens a block that keeps every following bullet, even after a blank line. Character bullets and section-note bullets become do-not rules, which SKILL.md treats as hard constraints on every frame, and the characters or section feels are lost.
M6b.evidence: test_do_not_label_does_not_swallow_the_bullets_after_it: 'Never show: blood\n\n- C1 The Keeper = V1...' gives the character bullets as do_not and no user C1. test_do_not_label_does_not_swallow_section_note_bullets: the '- Chorus: ...' bullets become do_not and no section feel is user. The r-words R3 test test_rw3_do_not_overcapture.py agrees.
M6b.suggested_fix: An inline label (`Never show: X`) is a one-line rule. A bare label opens a block that ends at the first blank line, heading, or line that parses as a character or section note.

M6b.location: src/mvh/stages/meaning/intent.py _DO_NOT_HEAD (heading regex widened by the N2 fix)
M6b.claim: The do-not heading regex matches never/don't anywhere in a heading. A title heading such as `# Never Let Me Go` or `# Don't Stop Me Now: my notes` therefore turns the story, the character lines and the section notes under it into do-not rules.
M6b.evidence: test_title_heading_with_a_do_not_word_is_not_a_do_not_block[Never Let Me Go] and [Don't Stop Me Now: my notes] fail: do_not is non-empty and C1 is not 'The Keeper'. A neutral heading gives no do_not and C1 'The Keeper'.
M6b.suggested_fix: Anchor the regex to the whole heading text (e.g. ^(never show|do not|don'?ts|avoid|no-?gos)\b.*$ with a short length limit) and do not apply it to an H1 title.

M6b.claim: `perspective` (narrator/addressee: who sings to whom) is filled from authored.json when the user does not give it, but the top-level field_sources has no entry for it. Under status 'user', an agent that follows SKILL §3 and RECIPES isDraft takes the draft's narrator and addressee as the user's direction. meaning.md prints it unlabelled too.
M6b.evidence: test_draft_perspective_is_marked_as_draft: with a user story plus the synth authored.json, status is 'user', perspective equals the draft's, and field_sources has no perspective key.
M6b.suggested_fix: Add field_sources['perspective'] (or perspective.narrator and perspective.addressee) set to user or draft, and label it in meaning.md and brief.md.

M6b.claim: The interview template always writes 'motifs: []', 'symbolism: []' and per-section 'do_not: []', although its docstring says it carries the user's answers so it 'can replace the free text without losing anything', and the template tells the user to copy it into intent.md. Copying the regenerated template back silently drops the user's section-level prohibitions, motifs and symbolism. The same loss happens to symbolism given as free text.
M6b.evidence: p3_yaml_roundtrip.py: YAML intent with S05 do_not 'No close-ups of faces here.', motif 'lanterns' and symbolism -> interview template -> rebuild: S05 do_not loses the user rule, motifs [], symbolism []. p2_roundtrip.py: free-text '## Symbolism' is lost the same way. Two failing tests.
M6b.suggested_fix: Prefill motifs (name/lines/note), symbolism, references, notes and every user section do_not in yaml_template (from intent/meaning user-sourced fields). Add a unit test that a parse -> template -> parse round trip is the identity for user claims.

M6b.location: src/mvh/stages/meaning/intent.py _parse_yaml / parse_intent; docs.py yaml_template palette line ('# hex (#1b2a49) ...')
M6b.claim: Hex colours typed the way the template comment suggests (palette: [#0e2346, #f2a541, rust red]) start YAML comments. Fenced (the form the interview shows): the block fails to parse and is also removed from the free text, so every answer, including the user's do_not rule and logline, is lost and the status stays pending. The warning wrongly says 'free text used'. Unfenced: the logline and do_not are lost, and the comment's example #1b2a49 becomes a user colour. Block list '- #0e2346': the items load as null and are dropped with no warning.
M6b.evidence: p4_hex.py: fenced -> form none, logline None, palette [], do_not [], status pending. Unfenced -> palette ['#0e2346','#f2a541','#1b2a49'], do_not [], logline None, status user. Block list -> palette ['#c93523'] only, no warning. Five failing tests.
M6b.suggested_fix: Before the YAML parse, quote bare hex tokens (#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8} after '[', ',', '- ' or ': '). In the template, show quoted hex (palette: ["#1b2a49"]). When a fenced block fails, parse it with the lenient region parser or line by line instead of discarding it, and never take colours from YAML comments. Warn on null list items.

M6b.claim: Do-not detection now captures too much. (a) Regression from the N2 fix: a label line ('Avoid: cliches.') keeps the do-not block open across blank lines and every following bullet. A list of section notes after a blank line becomes verbatim do_not rules, which are hard constraints copied to every agent, and the section notes are lost.
